{
  "IP": "neorv32_trng",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Generated random bytes",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "Fresh entropy bytes produced by the TRNG, sampled into words and buffered for software reads. The bytes have no entry port because they are generated internally and leave through the bus response.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The generated bytes may be secret and the read path exposes fifo.rdata through bus_rsp_o.data at line 117. The sampling and FIFO write path produces and stores the returned values, so unauthorized alteration of those elements can change the random bytes at lines 360 and 139-162. Deasserting enable clears the pool and the read control governs consumption, allowing the bytes to be discarded or withheld at lines 170-171.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker who tampers with the generator or FIFO path, or forces the enable, clear, or read controls, could learn, alter, discard, or prevent delivery of random bytes.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        360,
        366
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        117
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "TRNG enable setting",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The run-time setting that enables entropy generation and controls whether the random pool is retained. TRNG operation and availability depend on this setting.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "A bus write stores the incoming control bit in enable and that setting controls the generator and FIFO clearing, so an unauthorized write can alter the configuration at lines 105, 137, and 170. Clearing enable disables generation and causes the random pool to be cleared, which can block random-data service at lines 137 and 170.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could issue a bus write that changes the enable bit to disable generation and clear the available random data.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        105
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        95,
        105
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        109
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "Random-pool clear control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The bus-controlled command that clears the buffered random bytes. It affects whether already generated random data remains available for use.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The bus write value is stored in fifo_clr and drives the FIFO clear path, so an unauthorized write can change this control and discard buffered data at lines 106 and 170. Activating the clear path removes the random pool and can withhold required random data at line 170.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could set the FIFO-clear control in a bus write to discard pending random bytes and prevent their delivery.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        106
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        94,
        101,
        106,
        170
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Random-data read and consume decision",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The internally decoded one-cycle decision that consumes a random word from the pool for a data read. It has no entry or exit port because bus-request fields only decide it and it only controls the internal FIFO.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The decoded read-enable decision can be changed by the request conditions and controls FIFO consumption, so unauthorized manipulation can alter which random word is served at line 171. Suppressing or forcing this decision can block the required FIFO transfer or consume data unexpectedly at line 171.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "A malicious bus master could issue or suppress data-read requests to force unintended random-word consumption or prevent the pool from being serviced.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        171
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO availability status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The availability bit only reports or controls movement of buffered random data, so the buffer-status rule bars it as a separate information piece; the random data asset covers the relevant use at lines 112-117."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "TRNG debiasing and sampling sequencing state",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The debias state, valid flag, and sampling count only shape or sequence production of the random bytes, so the working-value and sequencing-state rules bar them as independent assets at lines 336-360."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Raw bus access command fields",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The strobe, direction, and register-select address only describe the access and are barred by the access-command-field rule; only the separately decoded fifo.re decision is retained at lines 103-108 and 171."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus response handshake and constant error status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The acknowledge repeats the request strobe and the error flag is tied to a constant, so the bus-handshake-copy rule provides no independent information asset at lines 98-100."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Simulation mode selection",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "SIM_MODE is a build-time generic passed into the generator and cannot be changed or withheld at run time, so it fails the build-time asset rule at lines 132 and 288."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO depth configuration",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "TRNG_FIFO fixes the FIFO depth at build time and no run-time element can modify it, so it fails the build-time asset rule at lines 22 and 147."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset timing",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The clock and reset only time or initialize the design and are excluded as conceptual assets by the clock-and-reset rule at lines 25-26 and 90-96."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: Fresh entropy bytes produced by the TRNG, sampled into words and buffered for software reads. The bytes have no entry port because they are generated internally and leave through the bus response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The generated bytes may be secret and the read path exposes fifo.rdata through bus_rsp_o.data at line 117. The sampling and FIFO write path produces and stores the returned values, so unauthorized alteration of those elements can change the random bytes at lines 360 and 139-162. Deasserting enable clears the pool and the read control governs consumption, allowing the bytes to be discarded or withheld at lines 170-171.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker who tampers with the generator or FIFO path, or forces the enable, clear, or read controls, could learn, alter, discard, or prevent delivery of random bytes.

conceptual assets.information: The run-time setting that enables entropy generation and controls whether the random pool is retained. TRNG operation and availability depend on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A bus write stores the incoming control bit in enable and that setting controls the generator and FIFO clearing, so an unauthorized write can alter the configuration at lines 105, 137, and 170. Clearing enable disables generation and causes the random pool to be cleared, which can block random-data service at lines 137 and 170.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue a bus write that changes the enable bit to disable generation and clear the available random data.

conceptual assets.information: The bus-controlled command that clears the buffered random bytes. It affects whether already generated random data remains available for use.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The bus write value is stored in fifo_clr and drives the FIFO clear path, so an unauthorized write can change this control and discard buffered data at lines 106 and 170. Activating the clear path removes the random pool and can withhold required random data at line 170.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could set the FIFO-clear control in a bus write to discard pending random bytes and prevent their delivery.

conceptual assets.information: The internally decoded one-cycle decision that consumes a random word from the pool for a data read. It has no entry or exit port because bus-request fields only decide it and it only controls the internal FIFO.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The decoded read-enable decision can be changed by the request conditions and controls FIFO consumption, so unauthorized manipulation can alter which random word is served at line 171. Suppressing or forcing this decision can block the required FIFO transfer or consume data unexpectedly at line 171.
conceptual assets.attack: A malicious bus master could issue or suppress data-read requests to force unintended random-word consumption or prevent the pool from being serviced.

considered, not kept.reason: The availability bit only reports or controls movement of buffered random data, so the buffer-status rule bars it as a separate information piece; the random data asset covers the relevant use at lines 112-117.

considered, not kept.concept: TRNG debiasing and sampling sequencing state
considered, not kept.reason: The debias state, valid flag, and sampling count only shape or sequence production of the random bytes, so the working-value and sequencing-state rules bar them as independent assets at lines 336-360.

The strobe, direction, and register-select address only describe the access and are barred by the access-command-field rule; only the separately decoded fifo.re decision is retained at lines 103-108 and 171.

considered, not kept.concept: Bus response handshake and constant error status
considered, not kept.reason: The acknowledge repeats the request strobe and the error flag is tied to a constant, so the bus-handshake-copy rule provides no independent information asset at lines 98-100.
SIM_MODE is a build-time generic passed into the generator and cannot be changed or withheld at run time, so it fails the build-time asset rule at lines 132 and 288.
TRNG_FIFO fixes the FIFO depth at build time and no run-time element can modify it, so it fails the build-time asset rule at lines 22 and 147.
The clock and reset only time or initialize the design and are excluded as conceptual assets by the clock-and-reset rule at lines 25-26 and 90-96.
